subject: Multi-rail payment flow, FX markup ladder, and beneficiary bank statement request
messages:
From: Nora Chen <nora.chen@vendpay.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Multi-rail payments: example MT103 / intermediary charge patterns

Hi Dylan,

Quick note from the payments team at VendPay — we've noticed some variability on incoming wires from Redwood customers and wanted to align on how Redwood prefers to route collection flows so our reconciliation and fee allocation are predictable. A few specifics:

- We saw two invoices last month where the beneficiary received a gross amount but your originating bank's correspondent introduced a $22 intermediary commission that wasn't present on the remittance advice. That caused short pays on our side.
- For mixed-currency invoices (EUR line items + USD taxes) your current collection rail sometimes sends USD cover vs EUR nostro depending on the route. That changes who eats the FX conversion.

Can you confirm:
1) Redwood's preferred currency priority when multiple payable lines exist (e.g., prefer invoice currency nostro vs sending USD cover).
2) Whether Redwood will include explicit instruction tokens (OUR / SHA / BEN) and / or correspondent tag hints (56A / 57A equivalents) in the payment remittance so our bank can match and allocate intermediary fees correctly.
3) If possible, please share a sanitized MT103 or bank-statement-style sample showing the tag chain you currently receive — even a stub with the fields you populate will help our ops team.

We're happy to accommodate whichever approach minimizes FX leakage and short pays; we just need a deterministic mapping so our AP can code the fees to the correct GL and pass VAT documentation cleanly.

I've attached a short file with the two example payments that showed the issue (redacted).

Thanks,
Nora Chen
Head of Receivables
VendPay Ltd.
attachments: VendPay_202610_remit_examples.pdf (pdf)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Nora Chen <nora.chen@vendpay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-rail payments: example MT103 / intermediary charge patterns

Nora — thanks for the detail and the examples. Really helpful.

High level proposal from Redwood finance/ops to start the conversation:

1) Currency priority ladder (default):
   - a) If we have a matching currency nostro for the invoice currency in your region, route to beneficiary nostro (minimizes FX).
   - b) If not, prefer a USD cover payment via our primary correspondent (CorrBank A) with an explicit SHA instruction so intermediary charges are split (we absorb primary correspondent fees; beneficiary sees smaller, disclosed mid-bank fees).
   - c) Only as a last resort ask beneficiary to accept local-currency conversion on their side.

2) Instruction tokens: we can include explicit instruction field mapping on remittance. Our payments team can set OUR / SHA / BEN per-entity basis; default for external vendors will be SHA unless a contract mandates OUR. We can also include a custom free-text field that contains the upstream correspondent id (e.g., CorrBankA / CorrBankB) and a short internal trace code.

3) MT103 / statement stub: attaching a sanitized stub (Proposed_PayRail_Mapping_v1.xlsx) that shows how we populate tags and the trace we can put in field 121/72. If you need a raw SWIFT MT103 sample, we can produce one — but wanted to propose the mapping first.

Open questions for your team:
- Is VendPay willing to accept SHARED (SHA) as the default? If not, we'll need to switch to OUR on a per-vendor basis which would increase Redwood's costs for some corridors.
- For EU/SEPA vs cross-border USD flows, do you prefer us to always send the invoice currency where supported?

Action: Ben / Laura — can you review and confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with SHA default and whether there are specific top-10 vendor contracts that require OUR?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that speeds things up.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: Proposed_PayRail_Mapping_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, Nora Chen <nora.chen@vendpay.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-rail payments: example MT103 / intermediary charge patterns

Adding a few operational constraints from Finance:

- SEPA first: for EUR invoices to EU entities, we will default to SEPA where the beneficiary has an IBAN and the bank supports it — that avoids SWIFT intermediaries, so no mid-bank commission.
- BRL/INR/other emerging corridors: these often require a correspondent; in those cases we should flag invoices as "expect intermediary" in AR so VendPay can match short pays.
- VAT reclaim: please send the remittance reference that ties back to Redwood's invoice number (and VAT number where applicable). This is critical for your team to be able to reclaim VAT on bank fees in some jurisdictions.

Policy decisions:
- Default instruction: SHA (split) for public vendors; Finance will accept OUR for a small set of strategic partners after we sign off on incremental cost.
- Gross-up vs netting: if a vendor contract requires gross-up (Redwood covers all bank commissions), we will mark those vendors and take the cost to Cost of Goods Sold. Otherwise we leave as SHA and vendors manage mid-bank commissions.

Operational request (Nora): could you run one test receive for next week and send us the MT103 or the bank statement showing the tag chain for that test? We will then decide if we need to change default instruction for that corridor.

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Nora Chen <nora.chen@vendpay.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-rail payments: example MT103 / intermediary charge patterns

Thanks — that works for us. We'll schedule a single USD test cover and a EUR SEPA test next Wednesday. Attached is a sanitized MT103 sample that shows the 56A / 57A chain we see frequently and where the mid-bank commission hit in the narrative.

Two clarifying points before the test:
1) Can Redwood confirm the FX markup ladder you'll apply when you convert outbound: do you pass through market rate + 0.25% (example) or do you apply a staged markup that varies by corridor? Our AP team needs to know expected netting to estimate short-pay likelihood.
2) Please confirm the trace/reference field format so we can match automatically. If you can embed: REDWOOD_INV_<invoice number> in field 72 (or the remittance text), that will let our system auto-reconcile 95% of cases.

Attachments: MT103_sample_stub.txt (txt)

I'll send the test instructions and expected timestamps by end of day.

Best,
Nora
